turn.text:
Interconnect HQ and Branch over a GRE tunnel, then encrypt the GRE traffic with IPsec. LAN subnets 10.1.0.0/16 and 10.2.0.0/16.

Site notes: HQ firewall is `fw` (LAN 10.1.0.0/16 on eth1, transit address 100.64.0.1 on eth2). The Branch firewall (LAN 10.2.0.0/16, transit 100.64.0.2) is managed by the branch team and is already configured as the far end: GRE tunnel 172.16.0.2/30 towards 100.64.0.1, and strongSwan expecting an IKEv2 PSK ('S3cret!') connection that protects the GRE packets (transport mode, child `gre-esp`). strongSwan (swanctl, charon at /usr/lib/ipsec/charon) is installed on fw.
Plan: ip tunnel add gre1 mode gre local 100.64.0.1 remote 100.64.0.2 ttl 255; ip addr add 172.16.0.1/30 dev gre1; ip link set gre1 up; ip route replace 10.2.0.0/16 dev gre1; mkdir -p /etc/swanctl/conf.d; cat > /etc/swanctl/conf.d/gre.conf <<EOS; pkill -x charon 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; /usr/lib/ipsec/charon >/var/log/charon.log 2>&1 &

input.command: true # AGENT-ACTION[C06]: ip tunnel add gre1 mode gre local 100.64.0.1 remote 100.64.0.2 ttl 255
true # AGENT-ACTION[C06]: ip addr add 172.16.0.1/30 dev gre1; ip link set gre1 up; ip route replace 10.2.0.0/16 dev gre1

true # AGENT-ACTION[C06]: mkdir -p /etc/swanctl/conf.d; cat > /etc/swanctl/conf.d/gre.conf <<EOS connections { gre { local_addrs = 100.64.0.1 remote_addrs = 100.64.0.2 local { auth = psk } remote { auth = psk } children { gre-esp { mode = transport local_ts = 100.64.0.1[gre] remote_ts = 100.64.0.2[gre] start_action = trap esp_proposals = aes256-sha256-modp2048 } } version = 2 proposals = aes256-sha256-modp2048 } } secrets { ike-gre { secret = "S3cret!" } } EOS
